item.title: Ngige Trial: Witness testifies on presidential directives
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday continued the trial of former Minister of Labour and Employment, Chris Ngige, over alleged abuse of office and fraudulent contract awards worth N2.26 billion involving the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF). At the resumed proceedings before Justice M.A. Hassan of the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Abuja, the commission’s third prosecution witness, Onwusoro Maduka Iheamelam, testified on directives arising from a presidential investigative panel set up to examine the activities of the NSITF under Ngige’s supervision. The EFCC disclosed this in a post on its X account on Thursday, November 12, 2026. During cross-examination by defence counsel, P.I.N. Ikwueto, SAN, Iheamelam, a Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Special Duties and Intergovernmental Affairs, told the court that he was a member of the presidential investigative panel established to investigate the matter. He said he received a presidential directive to implement the President’s decisions arising from the panel’s findings, including directives relating to the procurement functions and other activities of the NSITF during the period under investigation. The proceedings also featured an exchange between prosecution and defence counsel over access to the witness’s statements. Defence counsel requested that the prosecution produce the original copies of the witness’s statements for examination. However, prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, objected, arguing that the defence should formally apply for Certified True Copies (CTCs) of the documents if it wished to obtain them. Ngige is facing an eight-count charge filed by the EFCC, bordering on alleged abuse of office and fraudulent contract awards valued at N2,261,722,535.84. The allegations relate to contracts awarded during his tenure as Minister of Labour and Employment and his supervision of the NSITF. Following Thursday’s proceedings, Justice Hassan adjourned the case until February 9, 10 and 11, 2027, for continuation of trial. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 13, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened Friday, November 13, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the informal parallel market, as seasonal year-end import and travel obligations continue to weigh on liquidity. Official NFEM and CBN Rates At the official window, early market indicators ahead of Friday’s formal trading session show the dollar trading around ₦1,344.30 to ₦1,358.34. According to the latest published data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) covering recent sessions leading into Friday, the official NFEM weighted average stood at ₦1,358.34 per dollar, while the interbank market closed at ₦1,364.00 per dollar. The official window experienced notable volatility earlier in the week, highlighted by a ₦10.50 single-session depreciation from ₦1,353.50 to ₦1,364.00—its sharpest daily decline since October 22. Because official NFEM closing figures for Friday are published by the CBN at the end of the day’s trading session, banks and corporate buyers are referencing the ₦1,358.34 benchmark for morning settlements. Parallel Market (Black Market) Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a wide discount to the official rate. Street-level currency dealers and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,380 and ₦1,432 for buying, while selling rates ranged between ₦1,390 and ₦1,442.25 per dollar depending on location, dealer liquidity, and transaction volume. Across major commercial hubs in Lagos, retail trackers placed morning quotations near ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,390 for selling, whereas high-demand street quotes in Abuja and select Lagos corridors held closer to the ₦1,419 to ₦1,440 range recorded over the past 24 hours. Depending on the specific trading corridor, this leaves an exchange rate spread of roughly ₦32 to ₦82 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and parallel market prices. Market Drivers and Reserve Buffer Currency analysts attribute the persistent pressure on the naira to heightened fourth-quarter foreign exchange demand from importers restocking for the festive season, alongside overseas travel expenses and foreign portfolio investment outflows. A firmer United States dollar in global markets has further compounded pressure on emerging-market currencies. Despite the recent softening in both segments of the foreign exchange market, Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain a critical stabilizer. Hovering near $54.9 billion—an 18-year high that sits comfortably above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion—the reserve buffer continues to provide the apex bank with substantial capacity to support market liquidity and manage sharp volatility through the remainder of the year. item.title: 2027: Tinubu deserves second term, Adeola declares
item.description: ….Sets two million votes target for APC in Ogun, pledges to consolidate Abiodun’s achievements By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State for the 2027 general elections, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has declared that President Bola Tinubu deserves a second term, citing what he described as the achievements of his administration in infrastructure, education and workers’ welfare. Adeola made the declaration on Thursday at the IBD/INUMIDUN Squad for PDA/PBAT/YAYI and All Ogun State APC Candidates Rally in Abeokuta, where he urged Nigerians to support Tinubu’s re-election bid. He said the President had demonstrated the courage and political will to take difficult decisions aimed at repositioning the country and laying a foundation for sustainable development. According to him, the ongoing reforms and development initiatives of the Tinubu administration should be sustained to enable Nigerians reap their benefits rather than be abandoned midway. “We strongly believe that his administration deserves a second term. President Tinubu has demonstrated the courage to take difficult decisions for the long-term benefit of our country, and the gains already recorded must be consolidated,” Adeola said. Highlighting some of the administration’s achievements, the senator cited the ongoing Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway projects, describing them as strategic investments expected to improve connectivity, facilitate trade and stimulate economic activities. He also pointed to the establishment of three federal tertiary institutions in Ogun State as evidence of the administration’s commitment to expanding access to higher education. On workers’ welfare, Adeola commended Tinubu’s efforts to address pension-related challenges and improve the welfare of retirees, particularly through steps taken to ensure the payment of outstanding pension entitlements. The APC governorship candidate subsequently declared a target of two million votes for the party in Ogun State in the 2027 elections, urging members and stakeholders to translate their support into electoral victories. He said the target covered all APC candidates, from the presidential election to the National Assembly, governorship and State House of Assembly elections. “We, as leaders and stakeholders in Ogun State, are committed to reciprocating the good work of our President through our votes. We are targeting two million votes for all APC candidates, from top to bottom. “We are resolute, determined and committed to achieving this target,” he said. On the state’s political future, Adeola advocated continuity in governance, describing the proposed transition from Governor Dapo Abiodun’s administration to another APC-led government as an opportunity to sustain the state’s development trajectory. item.title: How couple attempted to sell one-year-old son for N800,000
item.description: The Federal High Court yesterday in Calabar sentenced a couple to five years’ imprisonment each for attempting to sell their one-year-old son for N800,000. Read Also: Terror survivor delivers triplets, gets relief from Kebbi govt The convicts, Emmanuel Okechukwu Ogbodo, 28, and Peace Ufeabuchi Nnamonu, 22, were convicted on two counts bordering on conspiracy and attempted child trafficking. Delivering judgment, Justice Rosemary Oghoghorie convicted both defendants on the two counts and sentenced each of them to five years’ imprisonment on count one and two and a half years on count two, with the sentences to run concurrently. She further ordered that the sentences should commence from the respective dates of their arrest. According to the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), Cross River Command, the couple had attempted to sell their one-year-old son to a third party for N800,000. The agency said it received a tip-off from the intended buyer, who reported the transaction, prompting its intervention and leading to the interception of the proposed sale. The convicts pleaded guilty to the two-count charge filed on October 12 and were arraigned on November 3. They were charged under Sections 27 and 29 of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015. item.title: Terror survivor delivers triplets, gets relief from Kebbi govt
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu BIRNIN KEBBI — A woman displaced by banditry in Kebbi State, Hindatu Lauwali, has received relief assistance from the state government after giving birth to triplets in Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area. The government provided her with food items, mattresses and other essential materials following a directive by Governor Nasir Idris. Lauwali delivered two boys and a girl on October 25 at Danko/Wasagu General Hospital. The newborns were subsequently referred to the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Birnin Kebbi, where they are receiving treatment for neonatal jaundice. The Chairman of the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Alhaji Kabiru Bako Zauro, presented the relief materials, saying the intervention followed the governor’s concern over the woman’s circumstances. According to a statement made available to newsmen on Thursday by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ahmed Idris, Zauro said: “We received information that a woman, Hindatu Lauwali, who is a victim of banditry and currently resides in an IDP camp in Kwargiye community, Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area, had delivered triplets. “Following the report, His Excellency, Governor Nasir Idris, directed the agency to provide the necessary support to the mother. “Consequently, we have presented food items, mattresses and other essential materials to assist her and her family while her babies receive medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Birnin Kebbi,” he said. Zauro said the intervention was part of the government’s commitment to ensuring that vulnerable residents, particularly those displaced by insecurity, were not abandoned to their circumstances. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the newborns and expressed hope that they would overcome their health challenges. The SEMA chairman assured that the agency would continue to respond to humanitarian emergencies and provide necessary assistance to affected individuals and communities across the state. Lauwali, who is taking refuge at an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Kwargiye community, fled Ragam village following a bandit attack. Recounting her ordeal, she said bandits invaded and took control of her village, forcing residents to abandon their homes and flee in search of safety. She explained that the village head, Muhammad Ragam, intervened when her health condition deteriorated and arranged for her to receive medical attention. “When my condition worsened, a joint Da’awa group took me to Zuru Local Government Area for further medical attention,” she said. According to her, she delivered the first baby without assistance, while medical personnel at Danko/Wasagu General Hospital helped her deliver the remaining two. She said the medical personnel subsequently recommended that the newborns be taken to Zuru General Hospital for further observation and treatment. item.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde ABUJA—The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport, as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, disclosed this, yesterday, in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government has been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. item.title: 40% of premium bread bakers shut down in 2yrs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole At the backdrop of difficulties in the economic environment, about 40 percent of bread-makers operating in the premium category, have shut their factories in the past three years. This was revealed by the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria (PBAN) attributing the situation to rising energy costs, poor access to affordable financing and inadequate government support. They warned that the challenges were threatening the survival of businesses and jobs in the sector. PBAN President, Engr. Emmanuel Onuorah, speaking on the sidelines of PBAN’s 2026 Day-Out event in Lagos yesterday, said the association’s theme, “Baking Through the Economic Storm: Innovation, Efficiency and Growth for a Sustainable Industry”, reflected the difficult operating environment and the need for innovation, creativity and efficiency to sustain the industry. He said: “The past years have been very tough. Words cannot even express how we feel. Our businesses are struggling, businesses are going down, and members are closing. In the last two years, we have lost close to 40 per cent of our membership to economic pressures. “Energy is killing businesses. We are trying to innovate, be creative and improve efficiency because, without efficiency, there is no way we can remain in business.” Onuorah, a petroleum engineer with 25 years’ experience in the oil and gas industry, said the association was exploring alternative energy sources, including a hybrid system that would allow bakeries to switch between diesel and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). However, he put the cost of transitioning a small bakery to the hybrid system at between N40 million and N50 million, describing the huge capital requirement and inadequate CNG supply as major obstacles. He also disclosed that PBAN had explored solar energy solutions but abandoned the initiative after discovering that the proposed financing arrangements would cost more than what members currently paid for electricity. The PBAN president faulted the financial system for failing to provide affordable credit to businesses in the real sector, alleging that government-backed intervention loans were largely inaccessible to genuine operators. According to him, even when sought for a loan of N12 million to convert lighting and air-conditioning systems at his facility to solar-powered alternatives, the bank was asking for a 34 per cent interest rate and a 20 per cent counterpart funding requirement. “How do you expect small businesses to survive with interest rates of 34 per cent? We are not asking for free money. We are asking for single-digit interest rates that businesses can realistically repay,” he said. He also questioned the effectiveness of government intervention programmes for small businesses, arguing that politically connected individuals benefited more than genuine entrepreneurs. item.title: 2027 polls: NASS condemns electoral violence nationwide
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Gift ChapiOdekina ABUJA- AHEAD of 2027 general elections, the National Assembly has condemned the wave of political violence across the country. Read Also: * Who won Lagos in 2023? * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal While the Senate urged the security agents to apprehend whoever was culpable in such acts to serve as deterrent to others, the House of Reps resolved to investigate the attacks. Speaking with Vanguard, yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu(APC, Ekiti South), said: “President Bola Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this. “We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.” Meanwhile, the Reps in its resolution, sequel to the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Mr. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers, expressed concern over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country. In Katsina State recently, supporters of the All Progressives Congress, APC, travelling for a campaign flag-off in Funtua were reportedly attacked along the Yashi-Funtua route in October. A female member of the party was injured, vehicles were damaged, and the police subsequently announced 14 arrests. Also in Calabar, Cross River State, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, was attacked on November 4, 2026. Police confirmed damage to vehicles and announced the arrest of a suspect, while investigations continued. On November 7, 2026, one person was killed and five others injured during an attack on a political procession and rally organised by supporters of NDC, along Nnebisi Road in Asaba, Delta State. This came as the National Peace Committee said it recorded 60 election-related incidents within one month, including violence, intimidation and threats. At yesterday plenary, presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace. Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties. item.title: Wike targets 3m votes for Tinubu in Rivers
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State, directing members to recruit at least five new voters daily to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who inaugurated the council on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for Tinubu in the state, urging members to work hard, remain focused and pursue issue-based campaigns. He dismissed concerns over confusion surrounding appointments into the various committees, saying the list of chairmen and members of the subcommittees would be ready by Monday to enable them to commence work. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various subcommittees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. Wike expressed confidence in the president’s victory in Rivers, declaring that the task before the council was to secure the targeted votes. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Recalling a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio on the three-million-vote target, Wike said he had assured him that the figure was achievable through hard work. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it is easy,” he recalled. The minister urged council members to see their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, stressing the need for unity and discipline in the face of opposition provocations. He cited the position of the Olubadan of Ibadanland and former Oyo State governor, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who reportedly expressed support for the coalition during a courtesy visit by the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, National Working Committee. Wike said Ladoja had indicated that, but for his position as a traditional ruler, he would have joined the Rainbow Coalition, which he described as a platform for bringing together different political interests to secure Tinubu’s re-election. In his remarks, Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, described the new campaign council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that secured victory for Tinubu in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the President. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. item.title: Tompolo leads grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu in Jigawa, Zamfara
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—Grand Patron of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, PBAT, Door-to-Door Movement, Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has led a drive to mobilise voters for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Jigawa and Zamfara states, unveiling 56 campaign vehicles for the two chapters. The vehicles, 31 for Jigawa and 25 for Zamfara, were unveiled on Thursday at the inauguration of the Movement’s state chapters. Tompolo was represented at both events by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Chief Kestin Pondi. Pondi said the vehicles were meant to ease transportation challenges and help members reach more communities with information on the policies and achievements of the Tinubu administration. He said they would be placed under the control of the governors. Jigawa State Governor Umar Namadi and his Zamfara State counterpart, Dauda Lawal, joined Tompolo’s team in urging voters in both states to turn out massively for the President in 2027. Jigawa pledged to deliver two million votes. Namadi said the state remained firmly behind Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He described the 31 vehicles as a major boost to mobilisation and urged members to use them judiciously. The governor challenged party supporters to turn their enthusiasm into votes, reminding them of the state’s earlier commitment of two million votes for the President. Pondi thanked Jigawa residents for the turnout during Tinubu’s recent visit, which he described as a show of confidence in the President’s leadership. He urged them to vote for Tinubu and Namadi in 2027, insisting that both deserve another four years. He recalled that Jigawa and Zamfara were among the states that contributed significantly to Tinubu’s victory in the last presidential election, and urged residents to surpass that performance. Pondi also appealed to Nigerians to be patient with the administration’s economic reforms, saying the benefits would take time to reach individual households. He said the economy was stabilising and that state governments now had more resources to execute projects and pay workers’ salaries. In Zamfara, Lawal thanked Tompolo and the Movement for backing the President’s re-election campaign. He urged the state leadership of the Movement to take charge of its operations and promised the support of his administration, declaring that Zamfara was for the All Progressives Congress (APC). The National Coordinator of the Movement, Comrade Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, commended the people and leaders of both states for their support. He urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and take part actively in the general elections. Asuku told Zamfara leaders that Nigeria had the right people in positions at both national and state levels, a situation he described as unprecedented since the return of democracy. The duo, who spoke while addressing party faithful and mmmoth crowd, at the Lagos All Progressives Congress, APC, East Senatorial District Rally, held on Thursday, at the Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, said President Tinubu had laid a solid foundation for Lagos State over two decades ago, providing the blueprint for the state’s sustained growth and development. According to him, “The President deserves more than our votes. He deserves our prayers and our support. Similarly, the Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, KOH, said the purpose of the campaign visit to the district was to canvass support for all APC candidates, urging residents to come out en masse on election day to vote rather than stay at home. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process. item.title: INEC holds mock presidential election November 28
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) plans to conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28 to test preparations for the 2027 general elections, Chairman Joash Amupitan has said. Amupitan announced the plan at a conference at Chatham House in London on Thursday, held to discuss “Democratic trajectory beyond the ballot” ahead of the elections. He said the exercise would simulate the forthcoming presidential election and test the commission’s readiness to transmit results. “On the 28th of this month, we are planning a mock accreditation and voting across all the states in Nigeria, so that we simulate a presidential election and just be sure that we have gotten it right and that there will be transmission of result,” Amupitan said. He also said the commission had reviewed lessons from previous elections and taken steps to address identified problems, citing recent off-cycle elections, including those in Anambra and Osun, as examples of improvements in the electoral process. “Nigerians must trust me because I’ve done off-cycle elections, and you agreed the last election in Osun State, there was improvement, and I said every election is a lesson. 2023 election was a great lesson for Nigeria. The one we had in Anambra was another. So we’ve learned certain things, and as a commission, we sat down to address some of those issues, and we have taken steps one after the other,” he said. Amupitan said INEC was working to improve logistics so voting and result declaration could be completed promptly as he pointed to the Anambra election, where results were declared the day after voting. “We are trying to improve on logistics to ensure that everything is done within the day, and then result. Look at the way we did an Anambra election. By the following day, we declared the result,” he said. He also cited recent off-cycle elections in the Federal Capital Territory and Osun, where he said results were declared the following day and voters observed the functioning of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the transmission of results. “In FCT, the same thing. In Osun, that used to be a serious problem, that the whole world thought that the whole country will collapse with Osun election the following day, the result was declared, and everybody saw the functioning of B-VAS and the transmission of results,” Amupitan added. He said the mock exercise and other measures were intended to prevent a repeat of past problems, adding that transparency and the ability to audit the process were essential. “So those are things and steps that we have taken to ensure that we don’t go back to the mistake of the past. And like somebody said, it’s not about if this whole process because if the process is transparent and everybody can audit it.” The post INEC holds mock presidential election November 28 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria still needs a national carrier, by Adekunle Adekoya
item.description: RECENTLY, the Senate was debating issues relating to the need to revive Nigeria Airways, our defunct national carrier, or the one that became a sakamanje run under the Buhari administration, called Nigeria Air. The Senate rejected calls for the revival of Nigeria Airways and Air Nigeria, and instead urged the Federal Government to renegotiate and enforce Nigeria’s Bilateral Air Services agreements, BASA, with China to allow Nigerian airlines to operate direct flights to the Asian country. According to the Senate, there is the urgent need for a review of existing aviation arrangements to address the imbalance in flight operations between both countries and ensure that Nigerian carriers enjoy reciprocal access to China directly. The Senate also urged the Federal Government to explore ways of establishing a viable national carrier that would fly the nation’s flag to ease challenges confronting Nigerian air travellers rather than what it described as wasting time in discussing dead issues. The Senate also asked the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs to initiate diplomatic talks with China regarding business visa facilitation for Nigerian traders and reciprocal slot allocations to Chinese airports. Resolutions of the Senate penultimate Tuesday were a sequel to a motion titled “Enforcing the Bilateral Air Service Agreement (BASA)”. The motion was moved by the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North). The Senate then mandated the committees on Aviation and Foreign Affairs to ensure compliance and report back in four weeks. To all intents and purposes, the Senators seem uninterested in any effort by the executive to revive a national carrier for our country. There are many ways to look at it. One is the capital outlay that will be required to get a national carrier off the ramp and its aircraft into the skies. Another thing is whether the coming of a national carrier will in reality upset the aviation apple cart as it is now, or help bolster it’s fortunes. There are even more, but I would like the Senators to reflect and use the experience of Switzerland. Switzerland once had a national carrier called SWISSAIR; it flew here and had offices in many of our cities. It also provided employment opportunities for many Nigerians. Many of our textile traders, particularly those of Lagos Island that dealt in exotic lace fabrics and brocade, had a sweet run while SWISSAIR was here. They simply booked Lagos-Zurich tickets, and from Zurich, took trains to St. Margrethen, in Gallen, where the textile mills are and bought their goods. In the late 90s till early 2000s, a man called Philippe Bruggiser was Managing Director of SWISSAIR. Under him, the fortunes of the airline dipped, and it subsequently went under. But the Swiss love their airline. As the story went, every Swiss adult contributed money to refloat the airline. The new airline was called SWISS, and it was relaunched in March 2002. item.title: Curbing trans-Sahara human trafficking
item.description: The rescue of four Nigerian girls from a suspected prostitution ring in Morila, Mali, is another reminder that trans-Saharan human trafficking is not a path to prosperity. It is still a booming, predatory business in which traffickers, recruiters, “madams,” transporters and exploiters profit while young Nigerians lose their freedom, dignity and, sometimes, their lives. The victims include a 14-year-old girl and three young women from Okene, Kogi State. They were reportedly promised work in gold mining and shops, only to discover that the real “job” was forced prostitution. One survivor, Sekinat, said her phone and identity cards were seized on arrival; she was threatened with being sold or killed if she refused. The girls eventually obtained a hidden phone, used AI on WhatsApp to seek help, and were rescued through a joint intervention by Global Anti-Human Traffic Organisation (GAHTO) and National Agency for Prevention of Traffic in Persons (NAPTIP). Their ordeal mirrors the experiences of many Nigerian women and girls trafficked through the Sahara to Libya and, in some cases, toward Europe. Survivors have described hunger, thirst, beatings, rape, extortion, slavery, abandonment, death, detention and debt bondage as part of their horrific experiences. Many are locked up, forced to swear oaths, told to repay inflated travel costs, and repeatedly sexually exploited. The pattern is clear: the promised greener pasture becomes a trap, and the only consistent beneficiaries are criminal networks. Several questions demand urgent answers. Who recruited the girls in Kogi State, and who financed and coordinated their journey? How did they cross multiple West African borders without effective interception? Are the alleged exploiters in Mali still operating? What support—medical care, trauma counselling, education and livelihood support—will the survivors receive? Curbing the menace requires more than rescue. NAPTIP, the police, immigration authorities and diplomatic missions must investigate recruitment chains, prosecute organisers, and disrupt the financial flows that sustain trafficking. Nigeria also needs stronger intelligence-sharing and joint operations with Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, Niger, Mali and Libya, since victims are moved through several countries before exploitation begins. Prevention must begin at home. Young people and their family members should be taught to verify foreign job offers, avoid unofficial recruiters, and report suspicious advertisements. Schools, faith institutions, motor parks and community leaders can help expose the false promises that traffickers use. Most importantly, Nigeria must open real opportunities for its youth. Vocational training, digital skills, agriculture, creative industries, entrepreneurship, microfinance, job placement and affordable education can reduce the desperation traffickers exploit. item.title: BTO4PBAT ’27 targets 1m votes for Tinubu in Ondo
item.description: ….Group intensifies grassroots mobilisation across 3,933 polling units By Dayo Johnson, Akure The BTO For PBAT ’27 Support Group (BTO4PBAT ’27) has intensified its grassroots mobilisation across Ondo State, setting a target of one million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The Director-General of the group, Ogbeni Adojutelegan Adesuyi Gideon, disclosed this in a statement issued in Akure, saying the organisation would strengthen its political structure and deepen community engagement across the state. He said the group was working towards establishing a strong presence in Ondo’s 18 local government areas, 203 wards and 3,933 polling units ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to him, the one-million-vote target reflects the group’s political ambition and determination to sustain grassroots mobilisation ahead of the presidential election. Adojutelegan said BTO4PBAT ’27, under the leadership of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, was committed to building an organised, inclusive and coordinated political structure capable of engaging communities across the state. “Our political structure will continue to engage communities at the grassroots level as we work towards achieving our target of one million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Ondo State during the 2027 presidential election. “We recognise that meaningful political engagement requires continuous interaction with the people, an understanding of their concerns, effective coordination and sustained participation at the community level,” he said. The Director-General explained that the group’s activities would extend beyond election periods, noting that regular engagement provided opportunities to promote political awareness, encourage voter registration and strengthen participation in democratic processes. He described Tunji-Ojo’s leadership as an inspiration for the group’s emphasis on grassroots coordination, unity and political participation. Adojutelegan also underscored the importance of peaceful political activities, mutual respect among party stakeholders and effective collaboration across different levels of the organisation. He said the group would continue to engage stakeholders, community representatives, party members and supporters as part of its preparations for the 2027 general elections. BTO4PBAT ’27 reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the activities of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State, while encouraging eligible citizens to participate peacefully and responsibly in the democratic process. The group said its one-million-vote ambition would remain the central target guiding its grassroots engagement and political coordination ahead of the presidential election. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, retains a strong support base and has the backing to repeat his 2023 electoral performance in Lagos State. Doherty said this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, following an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos. He dismissed suggestions that Obi’s reception among Nigerians could be weakened by his defection from the Labour Party to the NDC, arguing that his appeal is rooted in his political philosophy rather than the platform on which he contests elections. “The idea of a new party is not something that we should hang our hat on anymore in our clime. Parties may be new, but the individuals involved are not new. “But the reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. Doherty warned against underestimating Obi’s political influence, saying such an assumption could prove costly. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. He said the resistance by NDC supporters to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting was evidence that the enthusiasm which characterised Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign had not diminished. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind. “We have laboured for this, and you cannot deprive us of it. And I think that spirit is alive and strong. To those who might think that, following 2023, people have lost some of that energy, I think, if anything, today should let us know that it is game on.” Attack On NDC supporters An injured NDC supporter during the attack by suspected thugs in Lagos Doherty also condemned the attack on the party’s town hall meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, describing it as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary.” Suspected political thugs invaded the venue on Thursday ahead of the arrival of Obi and his supporters. The attackers, said to be armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. However, NDC supporters resisted the attackers, confronting them and throwing chairs in an attempt to drive them away. The confrontation disrupted activities at the venue before security operatives intervened. item.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
item.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. If victory is on your side, what is the essence of creating a crisis? We will not fight or attack anybody,” he said. item.title: Kwara PDP Candidate Kawu Pledges ₦100bn Security Fund
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Kwara State, Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu, has pledged to establish a ₦100bn security trust fund and introduce a 13th-month salary for civil servants if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Kawu made the pledges in Ilorin during the public presentation of his manifesto, tagged The SBK Compact – Kwara People First, which outlines his proposed policies on security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic development. The former top civil servant also promised to create 200,000 youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities annually, alongside a ₦19.2bn agricultural production fund to provide affordable financing and inputs to farmers and cooperatives. He said the proposed ₦100bn security trust fund would finance intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, equip security agencies and improve coordination among security formations to address insecurity across the state. Kawu said his decision to prioritise security was informed by his visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area, where he witnessed the aftermath of attacks and the suffering of residents. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu “One of the most painful experiences in my entire life was my visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of our state. I stood before the destruction. I saw blood on the ground. I witnessed firsthand the pain and fear of a traumatised community,” he said. He added that the experience reinforced his determination to ensure that residents could live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. “As Governor, I will not rest or sleep when the life of any Kwaran is under threat,” the PDP candidate said. On workers’ welfare, Kawu promised to introduce a 13th-month salary for all civil servants in the state, assuring that salaries and other entitlements would be paid promptly. “As a retired public servant myself, I understand the sacrifices, expectations and challenges of workers. I will ensure the prompt and timely payment of salaries and other entitlements. Workers must not have to struggle or beg for what they have lawfully earned,” he said. The former civil servant also proposed a ₦9.6bn revolving loan scheme for market traders and another ₦9.6bn single-digit interest loan scheme for micro, small and medium-scale enterprises. He said his administration would establish a ₦3bn Women Enterprises and Empowerment Fund to provide affordable financing and business support to women-owned businesses, while at least 1,000 artisans would receive support grants annually. On grassroots development, Kawu promised to allocate ₦50m to each of the 193 wards in the state within the first 100 days of his administration, amounting to an initial commitment of ₦9.65bn.
